figures.finding: Irish TV drama is covered by the Irish Equity / Screen Producers Ireland TV Drama Agreement, signed 30 March 2016, starting 1 May 2016 for three years, for all artists on Irish TV drama commissioned by an Irish broadcaster or State funder (crowd, walk-on, stunt and dance-only artists excluded).

figures.finding: Irish Equity's members approved using UK Equity's collectively bargained agreements on international co-productions shooting in Ireland (April 2022), and UK co-productions in the Republic are done on the Pact/Equity agreement.

value.uses: UK Equity / Pact agreements on international and UK co-productions in Ireland

figures.finding: At the Abbey Theatre, the national theatre, actors and stage managers are employed under the Abbey and Equity House Agreement; its rates are not published.
figures.applies: Ireland, Abbey Theatre (Abbey and Peacock stages), current page read 2026-11-01.

sources.said: The standards of employment for actors and stage managers are underpinned by the Abbey and Equity House Agreement. This sets out standards in regards to terms and conditions of employment. All actors and stage managers receive a contract of employment

figures.finding: Irish Equity's published minimum theatre rate is €464.26 a week from 1 October 2008, for up to eight shows, with no per-show rate, seven-hour days, and overtime at 1/42 of the weekly fee; no later figure is published.

value.basis: 8 shows a week (Mon-Sat, Wed and Sat matinees); no per-show rate
value.overtime_hour: 1/42 of engagement fee; time-and-a-half to midnight Mon-Sat, double time midnight-9am, Sundays and public holidays (minimum one-sixth of weekly rate)
value.holiday: two days' pay per continuous four weeks

figures.applies: Ireland, Equity theatre engagements, from 1 October 2008 (the page was uploaded 2014; no newer rate is public).

sources.said: The Equity minimum weekly theatre rate is €464.26 as from 1 October 2008. The minimum theatre rate is based on 8 shows per week, i.e. Mon to Sat with matinees on Weds and Sat historically. There is no 'per show' rate so the Equity minimum always applies even if only doing 3 shows per week. … Each week is comprised of seven hour days excluding one hour meal breaks. … Hourly overtime rates are calculated on the basic of 1/42 of the artist's engagement fee.

figures.finding: An undated production guide (written around 2020, before the 2021 film agreement) put the Irish actor's minimum at €850 a day for a buyout, with a week paid as four days for five, while the Equity agreement was being renegotiated; it is not the agreement's own card.

value.as_of: undated, c. 2020 (page links a 2020 crew rate card; says the Equity agreement was being renegotiated)

figures.applies: Ireland, screen, c. 2020; superseded in form by the 1 February 2021 Irish Film Agreement whose card is unpublished.

sources.said: Actors' Rates (Minimum) Daily: 850 euro minimum for buyout. Weekly: 5-day work for 4-day pay. Equity agreement currently being renegotiated. For stunt performers, average 750 euro per day For Children/Minors - average rate 250 euros per day. A special Government licence is required for these performers.

figures.finding: The actors' union is Irish Equity, part of SIPTU, for professionals over 18 based in the Republic; joining needs paid professional work or an offer of it, or a recognised full-time training course of at least a year, and an application form with CV. Irish Equity shows its fees only to members, but SIPTU's rule book binds every member to the weekly contribution of its First Schedule (from January 2026: €5.50 a week on wages over €500, €4.00 over €325 up to €500, €2.80 up to €325, €0.30 unemployed), with an entrance fee of one week's contribution unless a sector committee sets a higher one.

eligibility: evidence of a body of paid work or an offer of paid work from a professional production company
intention to work full time with a body of paid work or a relevant qualification from a recognised full-time course of at least one year
current student on such a course (student membership)
value.how: application form + CV, then membership card

fees.source: SIPTU Rule Book (November 2025 edition, First Schedule effective January 2026), Rule 134 and Rule 9
fees.entranceFee: one week's contribution, or a higher sum fixed by a Sector Committee with the National Executive Council's consent
fees.note: Irish Equity's own fee page (irishequity.ie/fees/) is members only, so whether the Equity sector committee sets a higher entrance fee or the 1% rate is not confirmed.

figures.applies: Ireland, read 2026-11-01; contributions apply to every SIPTU member (Irish Equity is a SIPTU sector), from January 2026.

sources.said: Irish Equity represents Professionals in the Live performance and Theatre Sector in the Republic of Ireland who are over the age of 18 and are based within the Republic of Ireland. … To join Equity, you must fulfil at least one of the criteria below: Be working as full time professional on paid professional contracts Have the ability to provide evidence of a body of paid work or an offer of paid work with a professional production company. Have the intention to work as full time professional and provide documentation evidence of either a body of paid work previously undertaken or a relevant qualification from a recognised full-time professional training course of at least one years duration. Be a student graduate of a recognised full-time professional training course of at least one years duration. Be a current student on a recognised full-time professional training course of at least one years duration (Student Membership).
Step 1: Submit your completed application form, specifying preferred form of payment and CV Step 2: Once approved you will receive your membership card

figures.finding: Most Irish film and television work is in Dublin and Wicklow; Wicklow County Council counted 60% of Ireland's studio stage space in Wicklow (January 2022).

The vast majority of film and TV production in Ireland is in Dublin and Wicklow
